title: Phase 1 CPU Micro-Scale 7-Arm Proof-of-Life & Diagnostic Validation
scale: micro-small (0.98M) vs micro-large (2.85M), 80 sup + 20 RL steps, 600 train / 64 Reg1 + 48 Reg3 eval, seed=42
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 7430U (12 logical CPUs, 62 GiB RAM, CPU-only)
bugs_caught: I2-Hybrid train-vs-eval interface mismatch in phase1_pilot/eval/diagnostics.py (prepended 4 pure continuous latents + <think>/</think> delimiters during eval despite rollout_hybrid using thought_len blended steps directly, causing fake NLL=7.68, Hard-BPB=5.030, ECE=0.844, 4.71x FLOPs; fixed to <1e-4 parity with recompute_hybrid_logprobs_and_continuation and locked with regression test).

Missing torch.distributed init/broadcast/sharding/grad all-reduce in train.py and grpo.py when launched under multi-GPU torchrun (fixed and verified with 2-rank Gloo test) + missing rl/__init__.py exports.
lessons: Binary exact-match R1 (RL-R1) suffers 100% zero-variance starvation (sigma_zero_frac=1.00) on low-accuracy small models, whereas strictly proper Brier R3 (RL-R3, I2-Hybrid) maintains sigma_zero_frac=0.00 with bounded no-thought drift.

I2-Hybrid is the strongest small-model arm (Hard-BPB 2.271 vs B2 2.266, OOD pass@16 37.5% vs B1/B2/B3 31.2%, delta_nll_trunc=+2.732 nats), but running thought_len=6 on every target token yields 2.51x B2 FLOPs; Stage 1 needs sparse/adaptive inference triggering to hit <=1.0x B2 FLOPs.

At 0.98M params and 80+20 steps, delta_nll_swap remains ~0.000 across all arms even when delta_nll_trunc is strongly positive (+2.73 to +2.91 nats), confirming micro-scale validates pipeline invariants but cannot decide H1b.

title: Phase 1 Stage 1 H100 Core Pilot (160M vs 410M / 1.0B on 2B Stratified Tokens)

lessons: Prerequisite before launch: build one-command scripts/eval_stage1.py (BL-07) and configure adaptive/sparse inference triggering so small-model arms test <=1.0x 410M FLOPs parity.
